executionArgs.additionalInstruction: Use the real local Django API contract. Register users with POST /api/auth/register using a unique email per test and expect 201 with a top-level user payload only; duplicate registration returns 400 but may use field-level errors. Login with POST /api/auth/login and expect 200 with access in the JSON body plus refresh only in an HttpOnly cookie; do not expect refresh in the JSON body. Refresh with POST /api/auth/refresh using the refresh cookie from login, and accept 400 for missing refresh cookies and 401 for invalid refresh cookies. Logout with POST /api/auth/logout requires Bearer auth and returns 204. GET /api/auth/me returns a top-level user payload. GET /api/auth/sso/provider requires an authenticated default-organization owner or admin user. POST /api/graphs/ creates metadata only with {name, description?} and returns 201 under data; include the trailing slash for collection POSTs. To create runnable content, create a version with POST /api/graphs/{graph_id}/versions using {graph_json}. Use graph_json {"nodes":[{"id":"output-1","type":"output","name":"Output","config":{}}],"edges":[{"id":"edge-1","from":"START","to":"output-1"}]}; do not use start/end node types. POST /api/graphs/validate expects {graph_json, strict?}; responses are wrapped under data, and invalid graph content may still return 200 with data.valid=false. POST /api/runs/start expects {graph_version_id, input_json?} and returns 201 under data. POST /api/runs/engine-events is server-to-server only: use X-ForgeGraph-Timestamp and X-ForgeGraph-Signature, not X-Engine-Signature. Compute signatures with HMAC-SHA256 over `${timestamp}.` + raw body only when ENGINE_CALLBACK_SECRET is available to the test process; otherwise assert invalid/missing signatures return 401 and do not assert a valid callback. Use plain HTTP at http://localhost:8000 and do not assume HTTPS.
